back: The stages a product passes through from launch to withdrawal: introduction, growth, maturity (saturation), decline.
Low sales, usually a loss, informative advertising, few outlets, skimming or penetration price.
Sales rise quickly, profits begin, rivals enter, persuasive advertising, more outlets.
Sales peak and level off, profit highest, strong competition, reminder advertising, extension strategies.
Sales and profit fall; promotion cut, prices lowered, product may be withdrawn.
Action to delay decline and extend a product's life, usually in maturity.
New version or flavour, new packaging, new markets, new uses, new promotion, price change.
They cost money and only delay decline; useless if the product is outdated.

front: Axes of a product life cycle diagram?
back: Sales on the vertical axis, time on the horizontal axis.
